references.text: The Lord appears to Abram and promises the land to his descendants – the first land promise later confirmed and expanded in Gen 13:15.
God makes a covenant with Abram and promises him land from the river of Egypt to the Euphrates, a concretization of the land promise given in Gen 13:15.
God gives the whole land of Canaan as an eternal possession to Abraham and his descendants, confirming the promise in Gen 13:15.
The land promise is passed on to Isaac and his descendants, as a confirmation and continuation of the promise given to Abraham.
God repeats the land promise to Jacob at Bethel, thereby continuing the covenant promise given to Abraham.
The Lord shows Moses the entire promised land and reminds him of the oath he swore to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob – a fulfillment of the promise in Gen 13:15.
Stephen recalls that God promised to give the land to Abraham and his descendants, even though Abraham himself owned none of it – a direct reference to the land promise.
By faith, Abraham obeyed and went out to the land he was to receive as an inheritance, living there as a stranger in the promised land – a response of faith to the land promise.
Prophetic fulfillment of the promise of eternal possession of the land for God's righteous people.
Direct reference to God's act of giving the land as an inheritance, confirmed in the song of praise.
Connects the promise of eternal possession of the land with obedience and life in the land.
Theological parallel: The righteous will inherit the land forever, confirming the promise.
Excerpt from the same covenant creation: the relationship 'I am your God' establishes the land promise.
Confirmation that the land promise is based on God's oath to the fathers and is to be inherited.
Prophetic restoration of the promise to dwell in the land and be God's people.
Direct retelling and confirmation of the land promise to Jacob's descendants.
Transfer of the land promise to Isaac, confirmed with an oath to Abraham.
Call to take possession of the land as God's gift, direct fulfillment of the promise.
Direct retelling of the land promise to Jacob and his offspring.
Promise to bring Jacob back to the land, confirmation of the land promise.
Reference to the covenant and oath to Abraham and Isaac, confirmation of the land promise.
Reference to the oaths to Abraham, confirmation of the land promise in salvation history.
